entities.summary: Gaekwads, a Hindu Maratha dynasty of the former Maratha Empire who later, he emerged as a prominent maratha general and military commander under Peshwa Bajirao I. Its subsequent (erstwhile) princely state of Baroda in western India from the early 18th century until 1947. The ruling prince was known as the Maharaja Gaekwad of Baroda. With the city of Baroda (Vadodara) as its capital, during the British Raj its relations with the British were managed by the Baroda Residency. It was one of the largest and wealthiest princely states of British India, with its wealth coming from the lucrative cotton business as well as rice, wheat and sugar production.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Gaekwad dynasty played a significant role in shaping the economy of British India, particularly through its lucrative cotton business and agricultural production. Its wealth and influence contributed to the region's economic growth during the British Raj.
